findings.title: Extended Windows path aliases bypass protected-output validation
findings.trigger: Invoke an ordinary-path builder with an extended \\?\C:\... output naming a protected input directory or missing descendant; reversed extended-root/ordinary-output also reproduces.
findings.observed: Actual unmodified builders exit 0 and create ZIP, receipt and publication lock inside protected smoke or source/bjarkiLearn. The original runtime bytes are unchanged, but the new files change the sealed input inventory. The next completed validation and normal builder fail.
findings.root_cause: Path.resolve retains different ordinary/extended namespace anchors for filesystem-identical paths. Normalizing case on individual components does not unify those anchors.
findings.controls: Ordinary protected paths reject before writes; native-distinct Unicode siblings remain accepted. Private root reproduction confirms samefile and 14 original installation files unchanged.

findings.title: Unsafe payload entries can disappear before the rejection check
findings.trigger: A Windows extended-name supplemental file ends in a dot and has no ordinary canonical sibling, or a supplemental directory ends in a dot. Invoke the builder through its ordinary path.
findings.observed: Actual completed builders exit 0 with valid ZIP/receipt and unchanged completed seal/runtime, but omit the physical supplemental file or directory subtree from both archive and inventory. A matched ordinary docs file is retained.
findings.root_cause: Ordinary Path.is_file returns false for the unpaired file and ordinary traversal cannot enter the directory, so capture() never receives the entry and cannot apply its new rejection guard.
findings.history: The omission reproduces with exact archived r8 collection as well. It is a remaining gap in r9 rejection coverage, not a newly introduced omission.
findings.controls: Adding a canonical sibling reaches the expected rejection; explicit extended-root collection also rejects; ordinary supplemental payload bytes survive.

findings.title: [P2] Reject unsafe native entries before ordinary traversal can skip them
findings.body: When a physical Windows extended-name payload ends in a dot and has no canonical sibling, ordinary Path.is_file() returns false, so the loop never calls capture() and the new Win32-name guard never runs. A trailing-dot directory similarly appears in ordinary rglob but its subtree is not traversed. Actual completed-copy r9 CLIs exit 0, preserve the seal/source bytes, and publish a verified ZIP/receipt silently missing these docs payloads; a matched normal docs .txt is archived with exact bytes. Check enumerated names before ordinary native file/traversal predicates can lose them, so unsupported names reject rather than produce successful incomplete payloads.
findings.history: Silent omission also occurs in the exact archived r8 collector. This is a remaining rejection-coverage gap, not a newly introduced omission regression.
findings.trigger_scope: Uncommon native Windows extended-path entries, ordinary-path builder invocation, no canonical sibling for the omitted entry
findings.limitations: Does not establish missing evidence in the clean supplied ZIP, live-WoW behavior, native POSIX behavior, or a physical second-drive result.
findings.test_gap: test_generated_metadata.py 238-239 creates a canonical sibling for each unsafe name, making ordinary is_file true and concealing the bypass. All 19 existing cases pass.
